newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN STOCKS - factors to watch - August 1.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN STOCKS - factors to watch - August 1.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Taiwan stocks on Friday:
* The benchmark stock index is expected to tumble on the central bank's decision to tighten monetary policy by raising the rediscount and secured loan rates, brokers said.
* The central bank decided on Thursday to raise the rediscount rate to 5.25 percent from 5.00 percent, and the secured loan rate to 5.625 percent from 5.375 percent.

* Alex Chen, HSBC James Capel: "The stock market will definitely fall. It's obvious the central bank wants to clamp down on speculation -- not only in the forex market but in the stock market as well."
* Oliver Fang of National Securities: "The market always reacts drastically to something unexpected -- the index will fall at least 200 points at the open."
* But analysts said the government would not let the stock index freefall as a new cabinet is set to be formed on August 30 after a reshuffle on August 28.

* Alex Chen, HSBC James Capel: "Long term, the government can't affort to let the stock market fall freely. The ruling Nationalist Party cannot affort to lose public support for the sake of year-end elections."
* Finance Minister Paul Chiu on Thursday urged investors to watch the fundamentals in the rallying stock market, but declined to say whether share prices were overvalued.

* Taiwan's top economic planner on Thursday said some shares may have been bid up by speculators and that the stock index's surge through 10,000 did not necessarily reflect the island's economic strength.
* Brokers said fundamentals of electronics are strong, meaning the electronics sector should still be able to make further gains following a short-term correction.
* Securities authorities allow local trading of SIMEX and CME beginning Friday.
